priceOrientation.note: Source/5 evaluates moriarty-financial-expression-contract/4. Price<A,B,S> means mantissa/10^scale units of base A for one unit of quote B. financial-expression-types-v1.ts holds that value type. financial-expression-source-types.ts accepts the same Price spelling in source text. financial-expression-v1.ts LitPrice builds the value. expression-types-v1.ts repeats Price for the non-financial expression profile and is not the source/5 path.

primitives.description: applyAccrue divides principal times numerator by the accrual denominator. The interest increases accrued, outstanding, and liabilityIncurred. D2 requires ceil because the result increases a liability. AccrualRounding is stored on the obligation and the author can select floor or ceil. The truncating division is the floor path. The ceil path adds one when the remainder is nonzero. Source/5 uses this lifecycle kernel. The earlier repayment kernel has no accrual.
primitives.gapNote: AccrualTerms.rounding lets the author select floor or ceil. D2 requires ceil for interest that increases a liability. A floor selection is an open conformance gap.

primitives.description: financial-expression-v1 reduce evaluates FloorDiv and CeilDiv at one site. The program selects the constructor through floor_div or ceil_div. A price conversion multiplies an amount by a base-per-quote Price and then divides the scaled mantissa by 10^scale at this site. D2 requires ceil when the result is an amount owed, a fee, or a collateral charge. A negative dividend is adjusted so the remainder is nonnegative before a ceil increment. expression-v1.ts repeats this reducer and is not the source/5 path. Source/5 evaluates contract/4 in this file.
primitives.gapNote: The program selects floor_div or ceil_div at this reducer. D2 requires ceil when the result is an amount owed. The author can select floor. That selection is an open conformance gap.

primitives.description: The same reduce site evaluates FloorDiv and CeilDiv when the result is an amount a party receives. That includes a payout, a withdrawal, a refund, and a price conversion into a received amount. D2 requires floor. The program can still select ceil_div. Quantity division uses this same site. This row shares the division line with expression-obligation-division because the implementation does not separate the two roles.
primitives.gapNote: The program selects floor_div or ceil_div at this reducer. D2 requires floor when the result is an amount received. The author can select ceil. That selection is an open conformance gap.

primitives.description: convertNominal divides nominal times mantissa by 10^scale. applyOriginate uses that quotient as the settlement quanta the debtor receives from the creditor. D2 requires floor for a received amount. Conversion.rounding lets the author select none, floor, or ceil. none rejects a nonzero remainder instead of rounding. repayment.ts convertNominal is the same helper on the earlier repayment kernel. Source/5 uses this lifecycle copy. The repayment use of this division is repayment-settlement-conversion.
primitives.gapNote: Conversion.rounding lets the author select none, floor, or ceil. D2 requires floor for the settlement the debtor receives at origination. Another selection is an open conformance gap.

primitives.description: allocateNominal ProRata divides nominal times principal by principal plus accrued. The author can select the allocation rule but cannot select a rounding mode for this quotient. The quotient is the nonnegative truncating division, which is floor. D2 treats the principal discharge as a reduction of liability in the payer's favour, so the required direction is floor. The truncated unit is not posted to a protocol-reserve balance. It stays in the same nominal repayment as accrued discharge, and the nominal total is unchanged. repayment.ts allocateNominal is the same earlier helper and is not a second source/5 primitive.

applyRepay uses convertNominal to turn a nominal repayment into the settlement quanta the payer must fund. D2 requires ceil because that amount is a charge that discharges debt. The division line is the same convertNominal site as origination-settlement-conversion. Conversion.rounding lets the author select none, floor, or ceil. The earlier copy of this helper is repayment.ts convertNominal, which source/5 does not call.
primitives.gapNote: Conversion.rounding lets the author select none, floor, or ceil. D2 requires ceil for the settlement the payer must fund. Another selection is an open conformance gap.

defiformalConversion.formula: A positive quote-per-base mantissa M at scale s denotes M/10^s quote units per one base unit. The base-per-quote mantissa at target scale t is the directed reciprocal 10^(s+t)/M. The numerator is 10^(s+t). A receipt uses floor: numerator//M. An obligation uses ceil: (numerator+M-1)//M. The source scale and the target scale stay explicit. This is not a rename and not a second rounding of an already rounded reciprocal.
